questions.prompt: Fill the single type parameter in the Python 3.12 generic class header.
questions.explanation: Python 3.12 introduced bracketed type-parameter syntax for generic classes and functions, avoiding a separate TypeVar declaration for many cases. class Cache[T]: ... declares T in the class header and makes it available in the class's annotation scope. The new syntax requires Python 3.12+ unless a tool transpiles or otherwise handles it; it is not valid source syntax on older interpreters.

questions.prompt: Declare a generic pair alias using Python 3.12 syntax.
questions.explanation: Python 3.12 added the type statement for explicit aliases, including parameterized aliases. type Pair[T] = tuple[T, T] declares a generic type alias without TypeAlias or TypeVar boilerplate. The new type statement creates a TypeAliasType and is different from ordinary runtime assignment.

questions.prompt: Mark the method as intentionally overriding a base-class method.
questions.explanation: Python 3.12 added typing.override to tell type checkers that a method is intended to override a base-class method. @override above a subclass method helps catch accidental renames or signature drift in static analysis. The decorator primarily supports type checking; it does not dynamically enforce subclass method compatibility by itself.

questions.prompt: Walk the tree with pathlib's Python 3.12 API.
questions.explanation: Python 3.12 added pathlib.Path.walk(), which yields directory path, directory names, and file names while walking a tree. for root, dirs, files in base.walk(): ... offers pathlib-oriented tree traversal. The yielded file names are names relative to root, so join them with root when a complete Path is needed.
